bibliographic.title: Oxygen Vacancy Induced Structural Distortions in Black Titania - A Unique Approach using Soft X-Ray EXAFS at the O K-Edge

affiliations.text: Department of Physics and Engineering Physics, University of Saskatchewan, 116 Science Place, Saskatoon, Saskatchewan S7N 5E2, Canada

Beijing National Laboratory for Molecular Sciences and State Key Laboratory of Rare Earth Materials Chemistry and Applications College of Chemistry and Molecular Engineering. Peking University, Beijing 100871, China

bibliographic.abstract: Unknown changes in the crystalline order of regular TiO2 result in the formation of black titania, which has garnered significant interest as a photocatalytic material due to the accompanying electronic changes. Herein, we determine the nature of the lattice distortion caused by an oxygen vacancy that in turn results in the formation of mid-band gap states found in previous studies of black titania. We introduce an innovative technique using a state-of-the-art silicon drift detector, which can be used in conjunction with extended x-ray absorption fine structure (EXAFS) to measure bulk interatomic distances. We illustrate how the energy dispersive nature of such a detector can allow us an unimpeded signal, indefinitely in energy space, thereby sidestepping the hurdles of more conventional EXAFS, which is often impeded by other absorption edges.

funding.funder: Natural Sciences and Engineering Research Council of Canada

samples.sample_description: Oxygen deficient black titania prepared by an Alreduction method.

datasets.dataset_description: Absorption spectra recorded in fluorescence yield mode at room temperature using an SDD at the O K-edge.
